top_rules: SH-DIAL-07: in #!/bin/sh write pipefail only as '(set -o pipefail) 2>/dev/null && set -o pipefail' on one line; bare, '|| true', eval and 'command set' abort dash 0.5.12 (exit 2) or posh (exit 1), and correctness must never depend on pipefail in sh
SH-DIAL-09: never use $'..' in #!/bin/sh; dash -2/-6ubuntu5/-12, yash 2.52 and posh print the literal text and exit 0; use printf (GREP-2 stays even after ShellCheck master removes SC3003)
SH-DIAL-18: at most one shebang argument; '#!/bin/bash -e -o pipefail' exits 1 and '#!/usr/bin/env bash -e' exits 127 on Linux; env -S fails on busybox and coreutils 8.22; set options in the body

SH-DIAL-06: every unpinned bash script has a bash 3.2 floor; a pinned script declares its floor and runs the one-line BASH_VERSINFO guard as its first command, because bash 3.2 otherwise prints an error, exits 0 and prints wrong data

SH-DIAL-01/02: every authored file declares its dialect (shebang or '# shellcheck shell=' first line); shfmt 3.13.1 silently parses a shebang-less .sh as bash, so only ShellCheck SC2148 and the grep catch it
SH-DIAL-19: portability evidence comes from dash, posh, busybox ash or mksh runs, never bash --posix (5.2 accepts arrays, ${x,,}, <( ), [[ ]] and exits 0) or the author's /bin/sh

SH-DIAL-17: local in sh is allowed with the exact directive '# shellcheck disable=SC3043 # local: dash, ash, bash, mksh, yash, posh; not ksh93 (see header)'; installers use the rustup has_local probe, which keeps ksh93 running but leaks the variable

SH-DIAL-10/24: never read -d in sh (absent on every dash incl. upstream 0.5.13.5, yash, posh) and never decide a feature from a version string (dash has no --version; Debian backported pipefail only in 0.5.12-7)
surprises: Map error: yash 2.52 DOES support set -o pipefail (pipeline status 1); it lacks $'..', read -d and echo -n (prints -n). posh additionally lacks test -nt/-ot/-ef. Conflict 3's sentence about yash is wrong.
bash 3.2 with an unguarded 'declare -A' does not fail: error on stderr, exit 0, and silently wrong data (count=1 a=2 b=2). A header floor without a first-command guard protects nothing.

shfmt 3.13.1's manual says .sh implies posix, but its source and a run show a shebang-less .sh is parsed as bash (arrays accepted, exit 0); the format gate cannot enforce dialect for such files. shfmt 3.14.1 is current (2026-09-06); fleet pins 3.13.1.

ShellCheck master (unreleased) makes SC3040 accept pipefail and removes SC3003, so the first upgrade silences the dash-safety warnings while Debian 12/Ubuntu 24.04 dash (and every shipped dash, for $'..') still need them; upstream dash 0.5.13.5 built from source has pipefail and $'..' but still lacks read -d, and Debian unstable still ships 0.5.12-12.

Userland drift beyond the brief deserves W2-3 attention: busybox 1.37 timeout exits 143 (not POSIX 124) and has no env -S; uutils 0.2.2 (Ubuntu 25.10) breaks the spaced 'env -S "cmd args"' form; uutils 0.10.0 'timeout -s KILL' returns 124 where GNU returns 137; amazonlinux:2023 and opensuse/leap docker images have no findutils at all.

Map's 'xargs -r use on Linux only, no-op on macOS' reasoning is inverted: BSD xargs already skips empty input, so -r is harmless everywhere (verdict: use; macOS part unverified, read only). Also the fleet claim 'macOS /bin/sh is dash' sits at line 110 of quality-bash.md in 6 repos (ocx, grimoire, grimoire-vscode, grimoire-duo, index, .probe-libc), not 4.

top_rules: BVG-01/02: every unpinned bash script is bash 3.2.57; enforce with the F5 grep (marker-skip + 59 -e patterns, output = violation), because ShellCheck 0.11.0 flags 0 of 47 probes (shellcheck#2615 open) and the grep had 0 false positives on the 166 fleet files.

BVG-03/04: raise the floor only with `# bash-floor: X.Y` plus a guard-first prologue (3.2-parsable `[ ]` tests, stderr message, empty stdout, exit 69) as the first statement and never inside main() or any compound command with 4+ parse-time syntax; gate = `docker run bash:3.2 bash script` must exit 69.

BVG-05: constructs that fail only at run time (${x,,}, declare -A, mapfile, ${x@Q}, ${ cmd; }) may hide in an untaken BASH_VERSINFO branch; parse-time ones ([[ -v ]], |&, &>>, coproc, ;;&, unparenthesised case inside $( )) never can.
BVG-06: `bash -n` on bash:3.2 catches only 6 of 47 constructs (and falsely rejects correctly guarded scripts); it is a secondary gate, never the floor check.

BVG-08/07: a guard reachable by non-bash shells is the POSIX `case ${BASH_VERSION-} in '' | [0-3].* | 4.[01].* )` form (exit 69 on 11 interpreters; the BASH_VERSINFO array form dies exit 2 on dash/ash); a sourced library refuses with `return 69 2>/dev/null || exit 69`.

BVG-09: in set -e scripts never use bare (( )), [[ ]] or ( ... ) as the statement meant to stop the script: (( )) and [[ ]] abort from bash 4.1 (not 4.2), ( false ) aborts from 4.0, a function-tail [[ ]] aborts everywhere; write i=$((i+1)), [[ ]] || die, ( ... ) || exit "$?".

BVG-11/12: under set -u write "$@" not "${@}" (dies on 3.2) and ${a[@]+"${a[@]}"} not "${a[@]}" (dies on <=4.3); never put & in a ${v/pat/rep} replacement without `shopt -u patsub_replacement 2>/dev/null || :` (no in-pattern spelling is stable across 3.2-5.3).

BVG-14/15/18: probe shopts as `shopt -s inherit_errexit 2>/dev/null || :` (bare exits 1 under set -e on <=4.3); BASH_COMPAT/compatNN removes no feature and is never a portability tool; bash 5.3 features (${ cmd; }, GLOBSORT, source -p, trap -P) need a `# bash-floor: 5.3` pin because Debian 12/13, Ubuntu 24.04 and Alma 10 ship 5.2.x.
surprises: The set -e boundary for failing (( )) and [[ ]] is bash 4.1, not 4.2 as the topic map says (measured on 4.1.17; NEWS 4.1 item j and the bats-core gotchas agree).

Only 6 of 47 constructs fail bash -n on 3.2; Bash parses compound commands whole but scripts line by line, so a top-level syntax error stops only at its own line, while the same error inside main() prevents the guard in that function from ever running.

set -e; ( false ); echo after continues on 3.2 and aborts from 4.0. Five fleet statement sites such as `( cd dir && build )` rely on 4.0+ semantics and would silently continue on macOS: grimoire bootstrap.sh:60, www-setup server.bash:296,298, ocx env.sh:87.

${A[@]@K} and ${A[@]@k} silently print values only on bash 4.0-4.3 with no error, fatal bad substitution on 4.4-5.0 and 4.4-5.1, and `${y/b/[&]}`, `.*` globbing and GLOBSORT change output with no error across 5.1/5.2 and 5.2/5.3. No in-pattern spelling of a literal & is identical on 3.2-5.3.

ShellCheck's SC2207 steers agents toward `mapfile` (a 4.0 builtin, command not found on 3.2), and `"${@}"` (the style bats-core and direnv use) is 'unbound variable' on 3.2 under set -u while `"$@"` is fine. A 3.2-only parser bug also kills `$(case x in a) ...;; esac)` unless the pattern is parenthesised.

Fleet: the only script that names the 3.2 floor is setup-grimoire install.sh:94-96 (awk tolower instead of ${expected,,}); index golden-baseline.sh:250 (local -A) is run by hand per taskfile.yml:372, and bash -n on 3.2 passes it. top_rules: Never use a GNU-only or BSD-only userland form (sed -i bare or with '', readlink -m, grep -P, grep --include, find -printf, mktemp --suffix, date -d relative, stat -c unprobed) without a probe; run the denylist (red on plant 31 lines, green on twin and on the boundary twin).
Probe timeout, flock, sha256sum/shasum, realpath, curl/wget, tar, find, xargs with command -v before use: each is absent on 2 to 8 of 21 base images (unprobed.sh check, red on plant).
Use command -v, never which: which is absent on 8 of 21 images, and SC2230 only fires under shellcheck -o deprecate-which (default exits 0 on the plant).

Put LC_ALL=C on each order-observable sort/comm/join, not as a blanket export: uutils applies ICU collation for any *.UTF-8 name even when the locale is not installed, and a blanket export changes wc -m, cut -c, awk length and ${#x} on UTF-8 text.

Temp files: mktemp -d "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/name.XXXXXX" with trap cleanup EXIT plus trap 'exit 143' TERM INT HUP and work run as cmd & wait $!; bare EXIT trap leaks on TERM in 8 of 13 interpreter variants, TERM-handler-before-foreground-child leaks in every bash.
Atomic replace means mktemp in the destination directory then mv; cross-filesystem mv is copy+unlink (partial 1966080 of 419430400 bytes visible, inode changed), and Debian 13 /tmp is tmpfs.

Never parse stderr text or --version banners to pick a code path: uutils differs from GNU on 30 to 37 of 304 cases (error text, timeout -s KILL exit 124 vs 137, date weekday words, wc -m in C locale, mv -n/cp -n).

A verification that ends in a pipe must carry a plant canary: grep -r --include on busybox errors, the trailing grep -v hides it, and the check reads as clean (V3 false-green); use find DIR -type f -name 'GLOB' -exec grep ... {} + for busybox-safe checks and never assume rg (0 of 21 base images).
surprises: Ubuntu 26.04 is a mixed userland: sort/date/ls and most tools are uutils 0.10.0 but cp and mv are still GNU 9.7; 26.10 switches cp to uutils. Do not key on a single coreutils flavour per distro.

uutils selects ICU collation for any *.UTF-8 locale name, including non-existent ones (zz_ZZ.UTF-8), while GNU silently falls back to C: the same LANG=en_US.UTF-8 sorts by bytes on Ubuntu 24.04 and by ICU on 26.04 (and by glibc locale order on 24.04 once the locales package is installed).
GNU mv -n changed exit status between coreutils 9.4 (rc 1 plus message) and 9.5+ (rc 0, silent), and cp -n warns on Ubuntu's 9.4 and 9.7 but not on Alma 10, Debian 13 or Arch.
Default ShellCheck 0.11.0 flags only 1 of 18 planted GNU-isms (SC3037 echo -e); even -o all adds only which (SC2230). ShellCheck is not a portability gate.

The wave-1 denylist pattern false-positived on 'transactional-update --no-selfupdate -d run' (k3s install.sh:698) because date -d had no word boundary; fixed with two pipe-free -e patterns per command, and the planted boundary twin now guards it.

Base-image tool gaps are wider than the ledger said: which absent on 8 of 21 (not 7), find and xargs absent on Amazon Linux 2023 and openSUSE Leap, rg on 0 of 21, git on 1, python3 on 3; nixos/nix has no sed or awk.

top_rules: Pick the error model by script kind: bash `set -euo pipefail`; sh `set -eu`; installer `set -u` plus explicit `|| die` at every fallible call; sourced library sets no options; verifier script `set -u`, no `-e`.
Never rely on `-e` inside a function that may be called from `if`/`while`/`!`/`&&`/`||`: the body runs with `-e` off on every shell tested, so fallible steps end in `|| return`.
Never write `local x=$(cmd)`, `export x=$(cmd)`, `declare x=$(cmd)` or `readonly x=$(cmd)`: declare, then assign. SC2155 is mandatory; `local -r` needs a manual check.

Under pipefail, never pipe into an early-exit reader (`grep -q`/`-m`, `head`, `rg -q`): the writer status is 141, 397, 13, 1 or 23 (curl), and a multi-line `echo "$v"` of 10 KiB or more fails 200 of 200 on bash 3.2-5.3. CMK-CORE-05 stays as the CMake sibling.
In `#!/bin/sh`, set pipefail only as `(set -o pipefail) 2>/dev/null && set -o pipefail`; the direct form exits dash 0.5.12 with 2 and posh with 1.
Under `set -u`, expand a possibly empty array as `${a[@]+"${a[@]}"}` or behind a `${#a[@]}` guard (bash 3.2 floor); empty `"$@"` needs no guard except on posh.
Drop `IFS=$'\n\t'` from every prologue: no measured benefit, it breaks `read` and `"$*"`, and it sets the bytes `$ \ n t` on dash 0.5.12, yash and posh.

A sourced library sets no `-e`/`-u`/pipefail and never calls `exit`; to adapt, probe with `[ "${-#*e}" != "$-" ]`. Also guard `shift` with `[ "$#" -gt 0 ]` (not `|| true`) and read `$?` before any substitution in the same command.
surprises: curl returns 23, not 141, when grep -q closes the pipe under pipefail, so a 141-only SIGPIPE rule misses it; the multi-line threshold is about 8-10 KiB, not the 64 KiB pipe buffer.

ShellCheck 0.11.0 SC2311 goes silent whenever pipefail is set (`set -euo pipefail`), and SC2015 misses `|| echo` and `|| exit`; SC2337 is not released; issue 3522 (`$?` clobbered by a substitution) has no check.
`shift` aborts dash (exit 2) and ksh93u+m (exit 1) even as `shift || true`.
The map's claim that empty `"$@"` fails under `set -u` on bash 3.2 is wrong; only posh 0.14.1 fails. Empty `${a[@]}` does fail on bash 3.2, 4.0 and 4.2.

Only 2 of 15 read SC2310 sites are real hazards, and 47 of 69 hits are in two installer files with single-command predicates. SC2310 should be demoted to a reading aid. The reading also surfaced two fleet defects: `ocx/test/manual/announce-e2e/scripts/env.sh:244` (reports 'settled' when `gh` fails) and `ocx/test/manual/run-windows-activation.sh:39-46` (runs the gate with empty `-OcxBin` when `wslpath` fails).

A sourced library with `set -e` kills its caller at the next `false` on all 23 interpreters tested; zsh differs, with `! f` exiting under `-e` on 5.3.1-5.9. Four stopped docker containers from the last runs could not be removed.

top_rules: One status-preserving EXIT trap (rc=$?; trap - EXIT; cleanup; exit "$rc"), installed before the resource exists.
Never bind one returning cleanup function to EXIT plus signals; give INT/TERM/HUP their own handlers that end the shell.
CLI entry points re-raise from a FUNCTION with kill -s NAME "$$"; never inline, never a hard-coded exit 130.
Never compare $? to a literal >=129; use -gt 128 and kill -l (128+N in most shells, 256+N ksh93u+m, 384+N yash).
Always exit "$rc" explicitly in traps; bare exit is only POSIX-2024 conformant on some shells.
die() writes to stderr, takes a status, ends exit "$rc", and is called only in statement position: v=$(f) || die "msg".
Exit vocabulary by kind (Rust cli-contract table, installers 0-7, gates 0/1+64/65/66) declared in a # Exit: header; never assign 123-128 or >=200.
No ERR traps in #!/bin/sh; bash ERR only for diagnostics with set -E.
Trap names uppercase without SIG prefix; single-quote trap bodies (SC2064).
Never local v=$(cmd); declare then assign (SC2155).
surprises: Returning EXIT+signal handlers sit in 7 fleet files and upstream exemplars (docker rootless, fish, k3s); they continue after the signal and exit 0, saved only by errexit; www-setup install.sh:798-800 turns ^C into exit 3.
mksh runs the EXIT trap on INT/TERM then exits 0; the k3s-style 'trap cleanup INT EXIT' + 'exit $code' reports success on SIGTERM in all shells but ksh (15).
ksh93u+m 1.0.10 inline-string re-raise exits 0 silently, 1.0.4 exits with the bare signal number; yash status is 384+N and ksh93 256+N.
busybox timeout returns 143, not 124; xargs owns 123-127, so gate scripts under xargs see 123.
The brief's docker-install install.sh:809-813 cite is wrong (no trap there); the real pattern is rootless-install.sh:265.
Rust cli-contract lists 66/70 as never claimed while swift gate scripts use them; zsh native scopes EXIT traps to the function and zsh 5.0.8/5.3.1 ignore exit N inside an EXIT trap.

The 5.1 Parser::ParseFile on the real host is the authoritative syntax gate: PSUseCompatibleSyntax (TargetVersions 5.1, explicit, disabled by default) catches only 7 of the 11 plant files the 5.1 parser rejects and misses leading-pipe, trailing &, clean{} and ${a}?[0].
Gate PSSA on the diagnostic count, never the raw -EnableExit status: on Linux 255 diagnostics exit 255 and 256 exit 0.

Never write unbraced `$o?.Prop` or `$a?[i]` (silent $null on every engine, reads variable `o?`); and never read $IsWindows/$IsLinux/$IsMacOS or $PSVersionTable.Platform in 5.1-bound code - use [Environment]::OSVersion.Platform -eq 'Win32NT'.

Every Invoke-WebRequest/iwr/curl/wget in 5.1-bound code passes -UseBasicParsing (or sets $PSDefaultParameterValues['Invoke-WebRequest:UseBasicParsing']); Invoke-RestMethod is exempt (measured unaffected on 5.1.26100.9444); without it the call fails exit 1 under -NonInteractive and throws NullReferenceException with closed stdin.

5.1-bound and irm|iex-served .ps1 files are ASCII-only with no BOM: BOM-less UTF-8 reads as cp1252 (length 5), an em dash inside a string becomes a U+201D quote and breaks the parse, irm|iex decoding depends on the server charset, and a BOM breaks iex on 5.1/7.4/7.6 and a shebang (exit 127).

Write text files from 5.1-bound code only with [IO.File]::WriteAllText/AppendAllText and New-Object System.Text.UTF8Encoding $false (or -Encoding ascii for ASCII data); >, Out-File, Tee-Object write UTF-16LE+BOM, Set-Content/Add-Content write cp1252, -Encoding utf8 writes a BOM, utf8NoBOM is rejected, and Out-File -Append onto UTF-8 appends UTF-16LE.

Around native calls on 5.1 set [Console]::OutputEncoding and $OutputEncoding to UTF8Encoding($false) (defaults IBM437 / us-ascii turn e-acute into '?' and mojibake), otherwise keep native-bound text and all messages ASCII; add Add-Type System.IO.Compression.FileSystem before [ZipFile].
surprises: Unbraced `$obj?.Name` is not null-conditional on ANY engine (7.4.7 and 7.6.6 included): `?` is a legal variable-name character, so it silently reads variable `$obj?` and yields nothing; neither the parser nor PSSA flags it (needs an AST check).

PSSA Invoke-ScriptAnalyzer -EnableExit returns the diagnostic count, but on Linux the exit status wraps at 256: 255 diagnostics exit 255, 256 diagnostics exit 0, so a count-based gate passes wrongly at multiples of 256.

Invoke-RestMethod is NOT affected by the 2025-12-09 Invoke-WebRequest change on 5.1.26100.9444 (KB5129195), and -OutFile-only downloads are exempt too, but -OutFile -PassThru is affected; with stdin closed (GitHub-style -Command wrapper) the failure is a NullReferenceException, not the prompt message; the KB documents a $PSDefaultParameterValues bypass while the Learn page still says there is none.

A UTF-8 BOM breaks `irm | iex` on 5.1, 7.4 and 7.6 (U+FEFF stays in the string) and a BOM before a `#!` line exits 127, so the PSSA always-on PSUseBOMForUnicodeEncodedFile advice is actively harmful for installers; the em dash (E2 80 94) decoded as cp1252 ends in U+201D, a PowerShell quote, turning a harmless-looking string into a parse error on 5.1.

top_rules: PS-ERR-01 MUST: every native call whose failure matters is followed by `if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0)` or goes through an Invoke-Native helper that resets `$global:LASTEXITCODE = $null` first (fail-closed); `$ErrorActionPreference='Stop'` never stops on a native exit code (5/5 engine rows exit 0 with 'reached').

PS-ERR-03 MUST NOT: do not rely on `$PSNativeCommandUseErrorActionPreference` in anything that can run on 5.1; it is a silent no-op there (7.4+ only, experimental in 7.3), and with it on `if (native)` and `native | Out-Null` throw under Stop. SHOULD set it in `shell: pwsh` CI blocks with 2+ natives.

PS-ERR-06 MUST NOT: no `exit` in a script delivered by `irm | iex`; compute `$IsIex = ($null -eq $MyInvocation.MyCommand.Path)` at script scope and use `return` or `$Global:LASTEXITCODE = n; break` (Scoop's shape). Exit kills the host on 5.1, 7.4.7 and 7.6.6.

SH-EMIT-08: the 36-case hostile corpus (20 wave-1 cases plus curly quotes, nul, nu_hash, trail_sq, datelike, big4k) is mandatory in every emitter's tests, executed in the real interpreter of each target and compared byte for byte, oldest and newest version.

SH-EMIT-14/15/16: data-channel order is no emitted code, then ASCII-only data parsed natively (nu `from json`, elvish `from-json`, pwsh base64), then a per-target literal; never `ConvertFrom-Json` on pwsh (ISO dates become DateTime on 7.4.7/7.6.6) and emit ASCII only for 5.1 targets.

surprises: zoxide does not belong in the curly-quote class: its PowerShell template interpolates only an alias name and quotes no value, so the wave-1 'same defect' claim for zoxide was inferred and does not hold; direnv 2.37.1 and mise 2026.10.2 do reproduce end to end (payload runs on pwsh 7.4.7 and 7.6.6), and starship only breaks on an install path containing U+2019 (parse error).

On Windows PowerShell 5.1 the curly-quote injection depends on the decode path: default IBM437 native pipe or BOM-less Get-Content mangles the character (corruption, no execution), while OutputEncoding=UTF-8, -Encoding UTF8 or ReadAllText UTF-8 execute it; non-ASCII literals in UTF-8 text fail on 5.1 and ASCII [char]0xE9 or base64 pass.

eval "$(emitter)" returns status 0 when the emitter fails (all 19 interpreter variants), so an emitter's refusal path (NUL, empty on pwsh) is silently lost unless consumers use out=$(tool) || return; NUL itself is silently truncated to 'ab' by dash, ash, mksh, posh and every bash.

top_rules: SH-CI-01: every workflow sets defaults.run.shell: bash or every run: step sets shell:. Unset means bash -e {0}, no pipefail. Fleet has 482 such steps, 22 with pipelines.
SH-CI-03: no attacker-reachable ${{ }} (github.event.*, head_ref, ref_name, client_payload, inputs.*) in a run body. Pass it via env: and read ${VAR} or $env:VAR. Proven by canary exploits under act.
SH-CI-04: never ${{ env.X }} in a run body. It is still template expansion, and both actionlint 1.7.12 and zizmor 1.30.1 miss it. Only the grep catches it.

SH-CI-15: gate = actionlint with SHELLCHECK_OPTS=--severity=warning, plus the SH-CI-03/04 greps or zizmor --min-severity high. actionlint misses inputs.*, pwsh bodies, composite action.yml and /bin/bash templates.
SH-CI-05/06: multiline GITHUB_ENV/OUTPUT values need a random delimiter, never a fixed EOF. Under shell: powershell (5.1) use Out-File -Encoding utf8 -Append, because >> writes UTF-16LE with a BOM.
SH-CI-07: every composite action run: step carries shell: and takes inputs.* via env:. Job defaults do not reach composites and actionlint does not lint action.yml.

SH-CI-12/13: in Taskfile cmds use set: [pipefail] or an inline set -o pipefail; in the same cmd, and inside status:. Never shopt: pipefail. Ban printf -v, PIPESTATUS, BASH_VERSION and unquoted '-' in assoc subscripts (panics through task 3.54.0).

SH-CI-18 (dated): ubuntu-latest becomes 26.04 between 2026-10-19 and 2026-11-19. Pin 24.04 or add a 26.04 leg. dash gains pipefail, bash goes to 5.3.9, uutils replaces GNU in the container, so test features and never grep --version for GNU.
surprises: actionlint 1.7.12 is silent on inputs.* (the fleet's real T2) and on pwsh bodies. actionlint and zizmor both miss ${{ env.X }} carrying untrusted data, and the payload executes. Only a plain grep catches all three.

www-setup test-installers.yml has 6 injection sites, not 2 (206,207,239,241,269,271). The 4 pwsh double-quoted sites execute a $(...) payload twice per line. zizmor finds all 6, www-setup's pinned actionlint 1.7.12 finds none.

The mvdan/sh assoc-array panic is an unquoted '-' in a subscript on write, read and compound assignment (even declare -A m=(["x-y"]=v)). It still panics on task 3.54.0 (mvdan 3.14.1). SH-CI-07 — Never put an attacker-reachable ${{ }} expression (github.event.* text fields, head_ref, ref_name, client_payload, inputs.*) in a run:/script: body; use env: and "${VAR}" / $env:VAR.

SH-CI-18 — In Taskfile cmds use no printf -v, PIPESTATUS, BASH_VERSION/BASH_SOURCE, or dashed associative-array subscripts in compound assignments (use a case).
